**Visual Analysis of Test Image:**
- **Affected part**: The cauliflower curd/head (not leaves)
- **Color**: Extensive brown/rust-orange discoloration covering the entire curd surface
- **Texture**: The curd appears soft, mushy, and waterlogged — the normally firm white tissue has decomposed into brown, wet material
- **Pattern**: Diffuse, whole-head rot without distinct spots or lesions with edges

**Differential diagnosis:**
- **Alternaria Leaf Spot**: Circular dark spots with concentric rings, primarily on leaves — does NOT match (this is head/curd rot, not leaf spotting)
- **Bacterial Soft Rot**: Soft, watery, brown decay of the curd — this is a textbook match. Erwinia-type bacteria cause exactly this mushy, brown, waterlogged curd rot
- **Black Rot**: V-shaped lesions on leaf margins with blackened veins — does NOT match (no leaf involvement visible)
- **Downy Mildew**: Yellow patches on upper leaf surface with gray/white downy growth on undersides — does NOT match (no foliar symptoms)

The extensive soft, wet, brown rot of the cauliflower curd — with no leaf spotting pattern — is characteristic of Bacterial Soft Rot.
